entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): omit completion token cap unless explicitly configured (#4091)
entries.note: One commit, five hunks, and only the last is a divergence — so the verdict is per hunk, not per commit. **(a) The fix itself needs no port: it stops deriving a completion cap when the model declares no output limit, dropping v2's `DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_CONTEXT_FALLBACK = 32000` and the `reservedContextSize` fallback (`llm-adapter/model/completion-budget.ts`). The fork never had that code path to fix — `llm/openai.rs:58-62` builds the Chat Completions body as `{model, messages, stream}` and emits no `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` at all, and `max_completion_tokens` has zero hits under `packages/kimi-agent/src`. The post-fix behavior (omit unless explicitly configured) is the fork's only behavior, so the 400s on strict serving stacks (bare vLLM) were never reachable here. **(b) The opt-out (`maxCompletionTokens <= 0` means 'no cap', `human/llm/protocol/format.ts`) has nothing to opt out of**: the knob the fork's docs advertise, `KIMI_MODEL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, appears only in `docs/{en,zh}/configuration/env-vars.md:179` and in no code file; `packages/kosong/src/provider.ts`'s `maxCompletionTokens` is type surface on a provider stack the fork no longer routes through, and its own comment points at an engine field that does not exist. Same 'docs half synced, code half not ported' class §6.8.2 already records for `KIMI_CODE_WATCH` / `KIMI_CODE_SEARCH_WORKER` / `KIMI_CODE_PERSISTENCE_MINIDB_READMODEL` — recorded rather than doc-edited, per that section's convention. **(c) The new `kimiUnsetCompletionTokens` provider trait (`human/llm-kimi/trait.ts`) supplies a default cap of `max(1, window - usedContextTokens)`; same as (b), there is no cap to supply. (d) `format.ts` also stops passing `usedContextTokens` when it is undefined — no-op here, the fork has no such field. **(e) Ported this round: `human/llm/requester/bases/anthropic/profile.ts` lowers `FALLBACK_MAX_TOKENS` from 128000 to 64000.** The fork's `llm/anthropic.rs::default_max_tokens_for_model` answered 128000 for a model id its ladder does not recognize, and its doc comment plus two tests pinned that 128000 as 'the TS provider's fallback' — stale the moment the constant moved. Now 64000, with the comment naming `21406fb4c8` as the reason. Anthropic's `max_tokens` stays mandatory on the wire (`anthropic.rs:196-200`); #4091 does not relax that, because the Anthropic API requires the field. **Side effect worth keeping in mind:** the fork matches by substring where v2 parses `family-major[-minor]` and rejects marker-less ids outright, so lowering v2's fallback made that pre-existing divergence **two-directional** — `relay-opus-4-1` is 32k here against 64k there, and `my-sonnet-4-6-clone` is 128k here against 64k there, where before this commit the fork could only ever be *below* v2. `my-opus-4-5-clone` is the one relay id where the two now coincide. All three are pinned in `default_max_tokens_agrees_with_v2_on_every_real_claude_id`. **2026-11-04 复核修正（A1 缺口）**：上文「fork 从不发送 max_tokens / max_completion_tokens」与实测不符——`llm/http.rs::completion_cap` 当时把「无声明上限」依次回落到 Anthropic 默认上限、`max_context_tokens`、`DEFAULT_FALLBACK = 32000`，四条 wire 构建路径都以 `Some(cap)` 下发（openai 的 `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens`、responses 的 `max_output_tokens`、google 的 `maxOutputTokens`）。现已按上游语义改为 `Option<u32>`：仅显式配置（`max_tokens`/`maxOutputSize`）才下发，`<= 0` 为 opt-out 不下发；未配置时仅 kimi 的 openai/openai_responses trait 以 `max(1, window - used)` 填充（`kimiAnthropicTrait` 无此钩子，Anthropic 仍以模型上限作为必填 `max_tokens`）。测试：`llm::http::tests::completion_cap_is_absent_unless_explicitly_configured` 与 `unconfigured_completion_budget_stays_off_the_wire`（先 RED 后绿）。

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): clear inherited cron tasks at the fork record (#4083)
entries.note: The mechanism it fixes does not exist here, and the fork has **two** cron surfaces — neither is session-scoped. v2 persists cron tasks as `cron.add` records in the session journal, so a fork — which copies that journal — inherited them and fired them from both sessions. In the fork: (1) **`fork_session` copies no state at all.** `session/sqlite_store.rs:834-861` does `load_session_history` -> `create_session_with_workspace` -> `UPDATE sessions SET parent_session_id` -> `save_turn(new_session_id, "turn-fork", 1, &history, None, None)`, with zero references to `state_entries` or `wire_events`. Both fork entry points go through it (`acp/mod.rs:1015`, `server/mod.rs:5130`), and the `btw` side channel does not fork a session at all — `napi_bindings.rs:3167-3170` seeds an in-memory subagent from `session.snapshot_history()`. (2) **The server-scoped surface is not per-session.** `server/mod.rs:595-599` documents entries under state key `("cron", "entries")`; `put_state` (`session/sqlite_store.rs:1336`) writes without a `session_id`, so the row stays NULL-owned and shared. (3) **The model-facing surface is not in the session store at all** — it is the workspace-keyed file store, `<home>/.kimi-code/engine-state/<workspace-key>/state/cron.json` (`storage/paths.rs:3-7`, `storage/state_store.rs:3-7`), keyed by a digest of the canonicalized workspace path. (4) **Session-scoped state exists but never holds cron.** `state_entries` does carry a `session_id` column (`session/sqlite_store.rs:516-530`) and `put_session_state` (`:1356`) sets it, but every caller uses it for `metadata` or `agent_config` only (`acp/mod.rs:475,526,684`; `server/mod.rs:1155,1183,5263,6001,7252,7259,7345,7352`) — never cron. So a fork shares the workspace's schedule exactly as every other session in that workspace does, which is the design rather than the bug, and the `cron_fork_cleared` reminder has no counterpart because telling the model "this fork has no scheduled tasks" would be false. The commit's other half (moving the `Forked` event class from `features/goal` to `session/agentLifecycle`, and widening `CronModelState` from a bare `Map` to `{ tasks, forkNotice }`) is v2 module layout with no Rust counterpart. **Verdict re-checked 2026-09-29 against a refreshed `.tmp/v2-ref-upstream` (`f409caa21e`)** after the first pass read only `cronService.ts` and missed surface (3).

entries.note: **Followed (2026-09-24).** Reverts #3964, which this fork had ported (see §6.7). Upstream's stated reason is a product principle, not a defect: once a user trusts a repository, content inside it is the user's own responsibility, so the engine stops defending against it (PR #4013, `Root Cause: N/A`). Kept upstream and kept here: the fail-closed trust prompt and the lazy footer git detection — only the pre-trust window stays guarded.
